steps.title: Declare the hatch groups
notes: Hatching is always active (FLAGS.DEF, no on/off switch). It contains one hatch group for the volume and one for the core. Both are created by the same factory create_hatch_group, so they offer exactly the same parameters: pattern, hatch distance, sizes, rotation.
The empty {} means “use the defaults of the table” for the volume. The core overrides two of them: a coarser hatch distance of 0.12 mm.

lines: // Always active. hatch_offset (mm): distance between the innermost
// contour ring and the hatch area; negative values let the hatch
// create_hatch_group arguments: (parent, id, text, defaults, flags,
// offered patterns, with power optimization). Defaults not given here
// come from FACTORY.TABLE_DEFAULTS (e.g. hatch distance 0.1 mm,
// The core uses a larger hatch distance (0.12 mm) by default: the core
// is not visible, so faster settings are acceptable there.

steps.title: One table of defaults
notes: All hatch groups take their defaults from TABLE_DEFAULTS: 0.1 mm hatch distance, 10 mm stripes, 5 mm chess fields, 3 mm hexagon sides and 0.05 mm overlap between neighbouring stripes, fields and cells.

The rotation starts at 0° and adds 67° per layer. The limitation window (keep the lines away from the gas flow direction) is off by default; its direction 0° relative to the gas flow means lines across the flow.

lines: // MPBF background: 67 degrees has no common divisor with 180, so the
// hatch direction repeats only after 180 layers. Default window
// (off by default): hatch LINES perpendicular to the gas flow (gas flow
// angle + 90 degrees), 120 degrees wide -> the lines are never closer
// than 30 degrees to the gas flow direction (see pattern_rotation.js).
// limit_center_angle 0 relative to the gas flow = hatch lines perpendicular
// to the gas flow (hatch angle value convention, see pattern_rotation.js).
// Power range in W; vector lengths in mm that are converted to the
// return times for minimum and maximum power.
// 0.1 mm = 100 micrometers between hatch lines. The block sort
// values 0 mean "use the default of the host".
stripe_width: 10.0, stripe_overlap: 0.05, stripe_script_sort: true, stripe_alternate: false,

steps.title: A new angle on every layer
notes: Before an area is hatched, the angle of this layer is computed: start angle + layer index × increment. Layer 2 on the left is turned by 67°.
The value is an angle value for the ATU builtins: 0° means lines parallel to Y, so the lines run at the angle value + 90°. The compass in the corner shows the line direction.

The angle value also sets the order of the lines. With Optimized sorting (on by default) an angle whose lines would be exposed downstream is turned by 180°: the same lines, exposed against the gas flow. See Hatch rotation.

lines: // Hatch angle of this layer: start angle + layer index * increment
// (default 67 degrees), optionally kept inside a window, e.g. "never
// MPBF background: rotating the lines from layer to layer avoids that
// hatch lines lie exactly on top of each other. The material gets more
// uniform and the residual stress (which is highest along the scan
// direction) is spread over all directions. 67 degrees is a common
// choice because the same angle repeats only after many layers.
// A window that is off, has no valid width or is 180 degrees or wider
// does not limit anything: plain rotation plus extra angle.

steps.title: Pick the pattern
notes: create_pattern_hatch chooses the function of the pattern. Stripes cut the area into strips of stripe.width with createStripes; the hatch lines run across each strip, so no vector is longer than about the stripe width.
The reference point (0, 0) puts the stripe borders on a fixed grid of the platform: all islands of a layer share the same stripe layout.

lines: case 'meander': l_hatch = make_meander_hatch(a_area, a_cfg, a_ctx); break;
case 'stripe':  l_hatch = make_stripe_hatch(a_area, a_cfg, a_ctx); break;
case 'chess':   l_hatch = make_chess_hatch(a_area, a_cfg, a_ctx); break;
case 'hexagon': l_hatch = make_hexagon_hatch(a_area, a_cfg, a_ctx); break;
// Arguments: result, width, minimum width, overlap, length (0 = endless), angle, reference point
// Minimum width = 1/6 of the stripe width: narrower rest stripes at the
// area border are merged into the neighboring stripe (no tiny stripes).
// Reference point (0, 0): the stripe borders lie on a fixed grid of the
// platform, so all islands of a layer share the same stripe layout.

steps.title: Chessboard: two directions
notes: createRectangles cuts the area into square fields that are rotated with the hatch angle. splitCheckerboard sorts them into the two colours of a chessboard.
One colour is hatched at the layer angle, the other at +90°. The residual stress, which is highest along the scan direction, is mixed between both directions on a short length scale.

lines: // fShift 0: no row offset (a real chessboard, not a brick pattern).
// fMinArea = 1 % of a full field: smaller rest pieces at the area
// border are merged into adjacent fields.
// The field grid is rotated with the hatch angle around (0, 0).
// Split into the "black" and "white" fields of the chessboard.
let r_hatch = HATCH_OPTIONS.hatch_island(l_even, a_cfg, a_ctx.line_angle, a_ctx.gas_dir);
let l_odd_hatch = HATCH_OPTIONS.hatch_island(l_odd, a_cfg, angle_with_extra(a_ctx, 90.0), a_ctx.gas_dir);
// moveDataFrom appends the blocks (the source hatch is emptied).

steps.title: Hexagons: three directions
notes: In a hexagon grid three cells meet at every corner, so two directions are not enough. get_hexagon_group gives every cell a group 0, 1 or 2 so that touching cells never share a group.
Each group gets its own angle: +0°, +60° and +120°. The three shades of green on the left are the three groups.

lines: // Group 0 uses the main angle, groups 1 and 2 add 60 / 120 degrees.
let l_group_hatch = HATCH_OPTIONS.hatch_island(l_groups[g], a_cfg, l_angle, a_ctx.gas_dir);

steps.title: Offset: rings that follow the outline
notes: The offset pattern needs no builtin pattern at all: it shrinks the area again and again. Ring k lies at 0.5 · d + k · d inside the border, every ring is computed from the original area, and every second ring is reversed.
There are no line ends at the border, which helps small and thin areas; on a large area the outer rings become very long vectors.

lines: // The first ring lies half a hatch distance inside the area border.
// Ring k lies at 0.5 * d + k * d, so neighboring rings are d apart.
// Every ring is computed from the original area (no error build-up).
let l_ring_isl = ISL.offset(a_area, -(0.5 * l_d + k * l_d));
// The rings were collected from outside to inside; inside_out reverses

steps.title: The lines themselves
notes: Every pattern ends in hatch_island, which calls the builtin hatchExt2. nHatchFlagAlternating reverses every second line (the meander), nHatchFlagFixedZeroOrigin puts the lines on multiples of the hatch distance measured from the origin, so neighbouring areas line up.

The vectors get BSID 500 (volume hatch, 280 W, 1200 mm/s). The order shown on the left is the order of creation; ATU's block sorting can still reorder the blocks, and the hatch angle decides in which direction the lines of a block are exposed.

lines: // Flags are bits; '|' (bitwise OR) combines several flags into one number.

recipes.title: Use stripes as the default volume pattern
recipes.why: Large parts then start with short vectors instead of lines across the whole area.
recipes.result: New profiles show Stripes under Hatching › Volume hatching. Press Stripes in Try it to see the result; the core keeps meander.

recipes.title: Smaller chess fields
recipes.why: 4 mm fields instead of 5 mm: shorter vectors and a finer mix of the two directions.
recipes.result: The default of every hatch group that offers the chessboard changes to 4 mm. Check it in Try it with Chessboard and the field size slider. For one profile, change Field size in the dialog instead.

recipes.title: A denser volume hatch
recipes.why: 0.09 mm instead of 0.1 mm between the lines puts more energy into the volume.
recipes.result: Volume hatch about 86 J/mm³ instead of 78 J/mm³ (280 / (1200 · 0.09 · 0.03)). Only the volume uses this table value: core, downskin, upskin and supports set their own distance.

recipes.title: Rotate by 90° instead of 67°
recipes.why: Lines alternate strictly between X and Y. The pattern_rotation.js header explains the drawback: the directions repeat after only two layers.
recipes.result: Every hatch group defaults to 90° per layer. With 67° the same direction comes back only after 180 layers.
